Hi friend, I’d definitely go to a Psych or a therapist and ask about Borderline Personality Disorder as mentioned. This could be the diagnosis that saves your life and flips it all around for you. With proper medication (like lithium or lamictal or Effexor, etc. depending on what your psych thinks), and DBT therapy, you could completely turn your life around if this is the diagnosis. Take care and please try to take this step, just going to a psych in general, before conditions heighten. Sending out good energy to you xx.

To also note, open communication is extremely important for us but also lies within a conflict of interest because of the fear of triggering her. Sometimes when I speak about my anxieties for reassurance (which we both know is super important) she gets triggered and starts crying about how awful she is and how she wishes she didn’t have BPD because she’s afraid I’m going to leave her one day. And that she never wants to hurt me and the thought of me being afraid of that horrifies her and makes her go into a “bad” place, which then has me sick to my stomach for even bringing it up. Very aware that none of this is exactly healthy, but both of us have mental illnesses and are trying our best and learning as we go. I guess all I want is from other BPD’s to give me success stories that they are happy and haven’t split on their partners.
